bioprojects.title: Leishmania gerbilli strain:LEM452 Genome sequencing and assembly
NHGRI Large Scale Sequencing Program for Organismal Sequencing

assembly_info.comments:
Background:

The Leishmania gerbilli LEM452 (WHO strain identifier MRHO/CN/60/GERBILLI) was obtained from Professeurs Jean-Pierre Dedet and Patrick Bastien, University Montpellier, France.

Genomic DNA was prepared from nuclei isolated from parasites lysed using 0.5% NP-40, to minimize the amount of kinetoplast (mitochondrial) DNA, and was provided by Drs. Deborah E Dobson and Stephen M. Beverley, Washington University School of Medicine.

The input sequence coverage for fragment reads was 82X, while the final assembled coverage was 140X (fragments, 3 and 8kb) using a genome size estimate of 35Mb. The combined sequence reads were assembled using the ALLPATHS software (Broad Institute). This draft assembly was referred to as Leishmania gerbilli LEM452 1.0.2. This version has been gap filled and cleaned of contaminating contigs. The assembly is made up of a total of 492 scaffolds with an N50 scaffold length of over 377kb (N50 contig length was 57.0kb). The assembly spans 30.8Mb.

This work was supported by NIH grant AI29646 to SMB and by NIH-NHGRI grant 5U54HG00307907 to RKW, Director of The Genome Institute at Washington University.

For questions regarding this Leishmania gerbilli LEM452 1.0.2 assembly please contact Dr. Wesley Warren, Washington University School of Medicine (wwarren@genome.wustl.edu). Downloads of the sequence data are available via the TriTrypDB genome browser server. Funding for the sequence characterization of the Leishmania gerbilli LEM452 genome was provided by the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH).
